section_name: A consumer may invoke the consumer rights authorized pursuant to this section 16
body:
at any time by submitting a request to a controller, via the means specified by the 17

controller pursuant to Section 4 of this Act, specifying the consumer rights the 18

consumer wishes to invoke. A child's parent or legal guardian may invoke such 19

consumer rights on behalf of the child regarding processing personal data 20

belonging to the child. 21

(2) A controller shall comply with an authenticated consumer request to exercise the 22

right to: 23

(a) Confirm whether or not a controller is processing the consumer's personal 24

data and to access the personal data, unless the confirmation and access 25

would require the controller to reveal a trade secret; 26

(b) Correct inaccuracies in the consumer's personal data, taking into account 27

Page 10 of 25

the nature of the personal data and the purposes of processing the data; 1

(c) Delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer; 2

(d) Obtain a copy of the consumer's personal data that the consumer previously 3

provided to the controller in a portable and, to the extent technically 4

practicable, readily usable format that allows the consumer to transmit the 5

data to another controller without hindrance, where the processing is 6

carried out by automated means. The controller shall not be required to 7

reveal any trade secrets; and 8

(e) Opt out of the processing of personal data for purposes of targeted 9

advertising, the sale of personal data, or profiling in furtherance of 10

decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning the 11

consumer. 12

(3) Except as otherwise provided in Sections 1 to 10 of this Act, a controller shall 13

comply with a request by a consumer to exercise the consumer rights pursuant to 14

this section as follows: 15

(a) A controller shall respond to the consumer without undue delay, but in all 16

cases within forty-five (45) days of receipt of the request submitted pursuant 17

to the methods described in this section. The response period may be 18

extended once by forty-five (45) additional days when reasonably necessary, 19

taking into consideration the complexity and number of the consumer's 20

requests, so long as the controller informs the consumer of any extension 21

within the initial forty-five (45) day response period, together with the 22

reason for the extension; 23

(b) If a controller declines to take action regarding the consumer's request, the 24

controller shall inform the consumer without undue delay, but no later than 25

forty-five (45) days after receipt of the request, of the justification for 26

declining to take action and instructions on how to appeal the decision; 27

Page 11 of 25

(c) Information provided in response to a consumer request shall be provided 1

by a controller free of charge, up to twice annually per consumer. If 2

requests from a consumer are excessive, repetitive, technically infeasible, or 3

manifestly unfounded, the controller may charge the consumer a 4

reasonable fee to cover the administrative costs of complying with the 5

request or decline to act on the request. The controller bears the burden of 6

demonstrating the excessive, repetitive, technically infeasible, or manifestly 7

unfounded nature of the request; 8

(d) If a controller is unable to authenticate the request using commercially 9

reasonable efforts, the controller shall not be required to comply with a 10

request to initiate an action under subsection (1) of this section and may 11

request that the consumer provide additional information reasonably 12

necessary to authenticate the consumer and the consumer's request; and 13

(e) A controller that has obtained personal data about a consumer from a 14

source other than the consumer shall be deemed in compliance with a 15

consumer's request to delete such data pursuant to subsection (2)(c) of this 16

section by: 17

The appeal process shall be conspicuously available and similar to the process for 2

any action taken or not taken in response to the appeal, including a written 5

explanation of the reasons for the decisions. If the appeal is denied, the controller 6

section_name: A controller shall: 12
body:
(a) Limit the collection of personal data to what is adequate, relevant, and 13

reasonably necessary in relation to the purposes for which the data is 14

processed as disclosed to the consumer; 15

(b) Except as otherwise provided in this section, not process personal data for 16

purposes that are neither reasonably necessary to nor compatible with the 17

disclosed purposes for which the personal data is processed as disclosed to 18

the consumer, unless the controller obtains the consumer's consent; 19

(c) Establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, 20

and physical data security practices to protect the confidentiality, integrity, 21

and accessibility of personal data. The data security practices shall be 22

appropriate to the volume and nature of the personal data at issue; 23

(d) Not process personal data in violation of state and federal laws that prohibit 24

unlawful discrimination against consumers. A controller shall not 25

discriminate against a consumer for exercising any of the consumer rights 26

contained in Section 3 of this Act, including denying goods or services, 27

Page 13 of 25

charging different prices or rates for goods or services, or providing a 1

different level of quality of goods and services to the consumer. However, 2

nothing in this paragraph shall be construed to require a controller to 3

provide a product or service that requires the personal data of a consumer 4

that the controller does not collect or maintain, or to prohibit a controller 5

from offering a different price, rate, level, quality, or selection of goods or 6

services to a consumer, including offering goods or services for no fee, if 7

the offer is related to a consumer's voluntary participation in a bona fide 8

loyalty, rewards, premium features, discounts, or club card program; and 9

(e) Not process sensitive data concerning a consumer without obtaining the 10

consumer's consent, or, in the case of the processing of sensitive data 11

collected from a known child, process the data in accordance with the 12

federal Children's Online Privacy Protection Act 15 U.S.C. sec. 6501 et seq. 13

(2) Any provision of a contract or agreement of any kind that purports to waive or 14

limit in any way consumer rights pursuant to Section 3 of this Act shall be 15

deemed contrary to public policy and shall be void and unenforceable. 16

(4) If a controller sells personal data to third parties or processes personal data for 1

targeted advertising, the controller shall clearly and conspicuously disclose such 2

out of processing. 4

(5) A controller shall establish, and shall describe in a privacy notice, one (1) or 5

more secure and reliable means for consumers to submit a request to exercise 6

their consumer rights under Section 3 of this Act. The different ways to submit a 7

request by a consumer shall take into account the ways in which consumers 8

normally interact with the controller, the need for secure and reliable 9

the identity of the consumer making the request. Controllers shall not require a 11
